# Python-Markdown: Architecture Python-Markdown converts Markdown text to HTML. A `Markdown` object runs the text through a fixed sequence of stages. Each stage is a priority-ordered collection of small processor objects, and extensions add features by registering more processors into those collections. The core never needs to know which extensions exist. ## 1. Components | # | Component | Files | What it does | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | **Markdown class / public API** | `markdown/core.py`, `markdown/__init__.py`, `markdown/__main__.py` | Builds the pipeline (`build_parser`), loads extensions, runs `convert()`, owns per-document state (`references`, `htmlStash`) and clears it in `reset()`. `__main__.py` is the `markdown_py` command line, which reads extension configs from a YAML/JSON file. | | 2 | **Shared utilities** | `markdown/util.py` | `Registry` (the priority-ordered collection used by every stage), `Processor` base class, `HtmlStash` (raw-HTML store), `AtomicString` (text that must not be processed further), placeholder constants, `parseBoolValue`. | | 3 | **Preprocessors** | `markdown/preprocessors.py`, `markdown/htmlparser.py` | Work on the list of source lines before parsing: normalise whitespace, and pull raw HTML blocks out into the `HtmlStash`, leaving placeholders. | | 4 | **Block parser** | `markdown/blockparser.py`, `markdown/blockprocessors.py` | `BlockParser` splits text into blocks at blank lines and offers each block to the registered `BlockProcessor`s in priority order. The first whose `test()` accepts the block runs and adds elements (paragraphs, lists, headers, code blocks, quotes) to an ElementTree. If its `run()` returns `False`, the parser offers the block to the next processor. | | 5 | **Tree processors and inline patterns** | `markdown/treeprocessors.py`, `markdown/inlinepatterns.py` | Tree processors walk and modify the finished ElementTree. The most important one, `InlineProcessor` (priority 20), applies the inline patterns (code spans, escapes, links, images, raw inline HTML, emphasis) to the text of every element. | | 6 | **Serializers and postprocessors** | `markdown/serializers.py`, `markdown/postprocessors.py` | Serializers turn the tree into an HTML or XHTML string (`output_format`). Postprocessors then work on that string, mainly putting stashed raw HTML back in place of its placeholders. | | 7 | **Extension API and built-in extensions** | `markdown/extensions/__init__.py`, `markdown/extensions/*.py`, `pyproject.toml` | `Extension` base class with config handling. Each extension's `extendMarkdown(md)` registers its own processors into the registries of components 3-6. 18 built-in extensions (abbr, toc, tables, footnotes, wikilinks, ...). | **Who calls whom.** `Markdown.__init__` calls `build_parser()`, which asks each stage module for its default registry (`build_preprocessors`, `build_block_parser`, `build_inlinepatterns`, `build_treeprocessors`, `build_postprocessors`). It then loads the requested extensions and calls `extendMarkdown(md)` on each. `Markdown.convert()` then runs the stages in order: ```mermaid flowchart LR SRC[Markdown text] --> PRE[Preprocessors
lines to lines] PRE --> BP[BlockParser + BlockProcessors
lines to ElementTree] BP --> TP[Treeprocessors
tree to tree] TP -->|InlineProcessor applies| IP[Inline patterns] TP --> SER[Serializer
tree to HTML/XHTML string] SER --> POST[Postprocessors
string to string] POST --> OUT[HTML] EXT[Extensions
extendMarkdown] -. register processors .-> PRE & BP & IP & TP & POST PRE -. raw HTML .-> STASH[(HtmlStash)] IP -. inline HTML .-> STASH STASH -. restored by RawHtmlPostprocessor .-> POST ``` **Default registries** (name: priority; a higher number runs first): - Preprocessors: `normalize_whitespace` 30, `html_block` 20 - Block processors: `empty` 100, `indent` 90, `code` 80, `hashheader` 70, `setextheader` 60, `hr` 50, `olist` 40, `ulist` 30, `quote` 20, `reference` 15, `paragraph` 10 - Inline patterns: `backtick` 190, `escape` 180, `reference` 170, `link` 160, `image_link` 150, `image_reference` 140, `short_reference` 130, `short_image_ref` 125, `autolink` 120, `automail` 110, `linebreak` 100, `html` 90, `entity` 80, `em_strong` 60 - Tree processors: `inline` 20, `prettify` 10, `unescape` 0 - Postprocessors: `raw_html` 30, `amp_substitute` 20 Extensions slot in between these. For example `toc` registers a tree processor at 5, so it runs after inline parsing. `abbr` registers a block processor at 16 and a tree processor at 7. **How an extension is loaded and configured.** `Markdown(extensions=[...], extension_configs={...})` accepts `Extension` instances or strings. For a string, `Markdown.build_extension()` first looks for an installed entry point of that name in the `markdown.extensions` group. Otherwise it treats the string as a dotted path (`package.module` or `package.module:ClassName`) and calls the module's `makeExtension(**configs)`. An extension declares its options in `self.config = {'name': [default, 'description']}` before calling `super().__init__(**kwargs)`. `Extension.setConfig()` stores each value, and when the default is a `bool` (or `None`) it converts strings such as `"false"`, `"no"` and `"off"` with `util.parseBoolValue`. Processors read options through `getConfig()`/`getConfigs()`. **Per-document state.** One `Markdown` instance may convert many documents. `Markdown.reset()` clears the `HtmlStash` and the link `references`, then calls `reset()` on every extension that registered itself with `md.registerExtension(self)`. ## 2. Architecture decisions ### ADR-1: Every stage is a priority-ordered `Registry` of processors - **Status:** Verified. Upstream changelog for 3.0.0: "Homegrown `OrderedDict` has been replaced with a purpose-built `Registry`. All processors and patterns now get 'registered' to a Registry." - **Context:** Extensions need to add, replace or remove behaviour at precise points in each stage, without editing the core and without knowing about each other. - **Decision:** Each stage holds a `util.Registry`. Items are registered with a string name and a numeric priority (`register(item, name, priority)`), iterated from highest to lowest priority, and removed by name (`deregister`). Registering an existing name replaces that item. - **Alternatives considered:** the earlier homegrown `OrderedDict` with location strings such as `"_begin"` or `"` root. Inline parsing and all later structural changes are done on that tree by tree processors. Python-Markdown ships its own serializers (`to_html_string`, `to_xhtml_string`) to write it out. - **Alternatives considered:** pure regex string-to-string conversion (as in the original `Markdown.pl`); the project's own DOM (NanoDOM), which it used before 2.0. - **Consequences:** Extensions create elements (`etree.Element`/`SubElement`) and do not write HTML text. The same tree can be written as HTML or XHTML (for example `
` vs `
`, boolean attributes). Text that must stay literal is wrapped in `util.AtomicString` so the inline processor skips it. ### ADR-3: Raw HTML is stashed behind placeholders, not parsed into the tree - **Status:** Inferred, from `util.HtmlStash` ("stashing HTML objects that we extract in the beginning and replace with place-holders") and `postprocessors.RawHtmlPostprocessor`. No design discussion was found. - **Context:** Markdown allows raw HTML, which must reach the output unchanged. It would break the block and inline parsers if they saw it, and it is often not well-formed XML. - **Decision:** `HtmlBlockPreprocessor` (blocks) and the `html`/`entity` inline patterns store raw HTML in `md.htmlStash` and leave a placeholder string (`util.HTML_PLACEHOLDER`) in the text. After serialization, `RawHtmlPostprocessor` replaces each placeholder with the stored HTML. - **Alternatives considered:** parsing the HTML into ElementTree elements (fails on malformed HTML and changes the author's markup); escaping it (Markdown requires it to pass through). - **Consequences:** Raw HTML is never touched by Markdown processing. Every stage must keep the placeholders intact. The stash is per document, so `reset()` must clear it. The same mechanism is used by extensions that produce finished HTML (for example `fenced_code`, `md_in_html`). ## 3. Constraints Rules a change should not break. The file shows where each can be seen. 1. **New extensions subclass `markdown.extensions.Extension`, implement `extendMarkdown(md)`, and their module defines `makeExtension(**kwargs)`.** Every built-in extension module does this. (`markdown/extensions/__init__.py`, `class Extension`, and the end of each `markdown/extensions/*.py`) 2. **Extensions change behaviour only by registering processors in `md`'s registries** (`md.preprocessors`, `md.parser.blockprocessors`, `md.inlinePatterns`, `md.treeprocessors`, `md.postprocessors`) with a name and a priority. They do not edit `Markdown.convert()` or the default `build_*` functions. (`markdown/core.py`, `convert()`; `markdown/util.py`, `Registry.register`) 3. **Core modules do not import from `markdown.extensions`.** Dependencies point from extensions to the core. The only exception is that `core.py` and `__init__.py` import the `Extension` base class. (`markdown/core.py:33`; the stage modules import only `util`, `blockparser`, `htmlparser`, `inlinepatterns`) 4. **Every built-in extension has an entry point in `pyproject.toml`** under `[project.entry-points.'markdown.extensions']`. That is what lets users load it by short name, e.g. `extensions=['toc']`. (`pyproject.toml`; looked up in `markdown/core.py`, `build_extension`) 5. **Per-document state must be cleared on `reset()`.** An extension that keeps state between calls registers itself with `md.registerExtension(self)` and defines `reset()`. (`markdown/core.py`, `reset()`; e.g. `markdown/extensions/abbr.py`, `toc.py`, `footnotes.py`) __init__.py abbr.py admonition.py attr_list.py codehilite.py def_list.py extra.py fenced_code.py footnotes.py legacy_attrs.py legacy_em.py md_in_html.py meta.py nl2br.py sane_lists.py smarty.py tables.py toc.py wikilinks.py --- title: Changelog toc_depth: 2 --- # Python-Markdown Changelog All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file. The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres to the [Python Version Specification](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/). See the [Contributing Guide](contributing.md) for details. ## [Unreleased] ### Fixed * Support automatic links with URL schemes other than HTTP and FTP, such as `` (#1244). * Fix quadratic-time id generation in the `toc` extension when many headers share the same text. * Ignore glossary abbreviations with empty definitions after inline elements, consistently with abbreviations before inline elements. * Strip complete HTML tags with quoted `>` characters from `toc` labels and generated heading IDs. * Fix quadratic-time regex backtracking in `attr_list` when a block ends with an unclosed attribute list followed by a long run of spaces, e.g. a line consisting only of `{` and some text with many trailing spaces (#1656). * Fix quadratic-time regex backtracking in hash headers when a long run of `#` 207: self.inlinePatterns.register(pattern, name, priority-ind) 216: self.inlinePatterns.register(emDashesPattern, 'smarty-em-dashes', 50) 217: self.inlinePatterns.register(enDashesPattern, 'smarty-en-dashes', 45) 223: self.inlinePatterns.register(ellipsesPattern, 'smarty-ellipses', 10) 232: self.inlinePatterns.register(leftAngledQuotePattern, 'smarty-left-angle-quotes', 40) 233: self.inlinePatterns.register(rightAngledQuotePattern, 'smarty-right-angle-quotes', 35) 285: md.inlinePatterns.register(HtmlInlineProcessor(HTML_STRICT_RE, md), 'html', 90) 290: md.treeprocessors.register(inlineProcessor, 'smarty', 6)
